title: Los Angeles weather: Rain returns to Southern California as large waves continue to batter coast. Here's what to expect - ABC7 Los Angeles
text:
Los Angeles weather: Rain returns to Southern California as large waves continue to batter coast. Here's what to expect - ABC7 Los Angeles 
 24/7 Live Los Angeles Orange County Inland Empire Ventura County California Weather 
 Rain returns to Southern California as large waves continue to batter coast. Here's what to expect 
 Los Angeles and Southern California will see rain return Monday as a series of storm systems moves into the region. Monday, November 16, 2026 9:33AM Share Follow ABC7 on Google Este artículo se ofrece en Español LOS ANGELES (KABC) -- Southern California will get its first round of rain Monday as a series of storms moves through the region, bringing several chances for showers through the end of the week.
 Light, scattered showers are possible Monday into Tuesday, though rainfall amounts are expected to remain light. After a brief break midweek, another storm is expected to arrive late Thursday into Friday with the potential for heavier rainfall.
 Another storm moving in at the end of the week could bring more rain, with anywhere from 1 to 3 inches possible in some areas. Expect that Thursday into Friday.
 Meanwhile along the coast, high surf advisories remain in effect along Los Angeles County beaches through Tuesday, with large waves of 6 to 9 feet and dangerous rip currents expected. Officials advised residents and visitors to stay out of the water because of hazardous ocean conditions.
 RELATED: What is an atmospheric river? Meteorologist Dallas Raines explains 
 Monday forecast
 Los Angeles and Orange counties can expect a 50% chance of rain developing during the day and continuing into Monday night. Expect a high of 71 degrees and a low of 55.
 The valleys and Inland Empire will see Monday a 20% chance of showers, especially during the afternoon and evening, with a high of 70 degrees and a low of 53. Beach communities can expect a cloudy morning with a 30% chance of rain Monday. The area will see a high of 72 degrees and a low of 57. Elevated surf and dangerous rip currents will continue along the coast.
 Mountain communities will be partly cloudy Monday, with a high of 51 degrees and a chilly overnight low of 24..
 Desert areas can expect partly cloudy skies Monday, with a 20% chance of showers. Highs will reach around 64 degrees with a low of 37. Palm Springs is expected to see a high of 77.
